# Journal read-path parity corpus

Generated by `tests/helpers/journal_fixture_corpus.py` — do not hand-edit the fixture files (NUL bytes, invalid UTF-8 and multibyte payloads do not survive an editor).

Expected verdicts are CAPTURED from the BASE bash scanner by
`tests/packs/preflight_journal_parity_test.sh` and frozen in
`EXPECTED.json`; a BASE/helper disagreement is a helper defect,
never a correction of the fixture.

| fixture | what it pins |
|---|---|
| `01-canonical-empty-journal` | the initialisation shape journal_init writes; ACCEPT |
| `02-live-shaped-journal` | a realistic populated journal; ACCEPT |
| `03-empty-file` | 0 bytes -> the EMPTY pre-check (lib.sh:969-972); REFUSE |
| `04-truncated-mid-object` | unbalanced `{` + unterminated string; REFUSE (torn write) |
| `05-truncated-mid-array` | unbalanced `[` + unterminated string; REFUSE |
| `06-unterminated-string` | in_str=1 at EOF; REFUSE |
| `07-escaped-quote-in-string` | an escaped quote inside a value; the `esc` state machine; ACCEPT |
| `08-trailing-backslash-outside-string` | a standalone trailing backslash OUTSIDE any string: esc is never set, the counts stay balanced -> ACCEPT (BASE). The SAME backslash inside a string REFUSES (case 6 semantics) -- the fixture pins the position. Encode BASE, not the 'correct' behaviour. |
| `09-braces-inside-string` | string-awareness: braces/brackets inside a value are not counted; ACCEPT |
| `10-multibyte-utf8` | valid multibyte UTF-8 payload; byte-scan == char-scan; ACCEPT |
| `11-invalid-utf8` | invalid UTF-8 bytes: bash tolerates them, a json.loads helper would refuse -- this row is the D1-1 decision boundary; ACCEPT |
| `12-single-quoted-pseudo-json` | not JSON at all; proves the scanner is a STRUCTURAL check, not a parser; ACCEPT |
| `13-trailing-comma` | trailing comma; a strict parser refuses, the scanner accepts; ACCEPT |
| `14-top-level-array` | top-level array; the scanner counts brackets too; ACCEPT |
| `15-binary-garbage-no-braces` | no braces at all (ob=0 cb=0) -> balanced -> ACCEPT. Also exercises the NUL-drop: the stdout digest is the NUL-dropped echo. The most counter-intuitive row; the parity test's value is highest here. |
| `16-whitespace-only` | whitespace-only: non-empty after `$(cat)`, balanced -> ACCEPT |
| `17-newline-only` | newline-only: `$(cat)` strips ALL trailing newlines -> EMPTY -> REFUSE |
| `18-trailing-garbage-bracefree` | valid JSON + brace-free trailing garbage: the scanner scans the whole string and only counts braces; ACCEPT |
| `19-trailing-garbage-with-brace` | valid JSON + an extra `}`: ob=1, cb=2 -> REFUSE |
| `20-nul-inside-string` | NUL inside a string: `$(cat)` DROPS it (stdout digest is the dropped echo, stderr carries the warning class); ACCEPT |
| `21-duplicate-key` | duplicate key: read ACCEPT; `sub x` = FIRST occurrence (10); `update x 99` = the exact corrupt bytes {"x":10,"b":2,"x":99,"b":2,"x":20} (BASE-BUG-PRESERVING) |
| `22-escape-then-multibyte` | escape then multibyte (backslash + U+00E9) inside a value: the journal_update value scan's 2-character escape skip. MEASURED: the verdict is locale-invariant (C / C.UTF-8 / en_US.UTF-8 byte-identical) and the 2-char skip is behaviourally identical to a 2-byte skip (skipped bytes can only be continuation bytes, never a quote). |

## Guard boundary + processed-bytes pin (G1–G5)

| fixture | what it pins |
|---|---|
| `G1-guard-threshold-minus-1` | JOURNAL_SIZE_GUARD_BYTES-1 on the LEGACY class (helper absent) -> ALLOWED (the legacy walk is inside the 120 s step budget) |
| `G2-guard-threshold-exact` | exactly JOURNAL_SIZE_GUARD_BYTES on the LEGACY class -> REFUSE loudly (size-named row + non-zero rc) |
| `G3-guard-threshold-plus-1` | JOURNAL_SIZE_GUARD_BYTES+1 on the LEGACY class -> REFUSE loudly |
| `G4-guard-on-fast-path` | threshold+1 WITH the python helper present -> NO refusal (the guard is not consulted on the O(N) path: the next ceremony, which reads a 455 KB+ live journal, must never be blocked) |
| `G5-processed-bytes-divergence` | backslash + NUL before the closing quote: `$(cat)` DROPS the NUL, so the backslash escapes the quote, the string never closes -> REFUSED by the bash walk; a RAW-byte scan lets the NUL consume the escape flag and ACCEPTS. This row pins that the verdict domain is the PROCESSED bytes. Mutation-meaningful: a raw-byte helper turns RED. |

G1–G4 are consumed by `tests/packs/preflight_size_guard_test.sh`
(shell-level guard behaviour); G5 is consumed by the parity
harness (byte-level verdict). Together: 22 + 5 = 27 fixtures.
